citeAs: Badertdinov, I., Golubev, A., Nekrashevich, M., Shevtsov, A., Karasik, S., Andriushchenko, A., Trofimova, M., Litvintseva, D., Yangel, B. (2025). SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset of 21,336 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks extracted from real-world GitHub repositories, designed for training and benchmarking LLM-based agents, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches. Each task instance includes a GitHub issue, solution patch, test patch, and automated quality annotations. The dataset is built using a fully automated pipeline covering environment configuration, build setup, test validation, and quality assessment.
name: SWE-rebench
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Automated annotation using fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model; distributed computing platform TractoAI used for pipeline execution and parallel processing.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated quality assessment using a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model trained on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified. The model predicts three binary quality labels per task: Issue Clarity (whether the issue description is sufficiently detailed), Task Complexity (estimated effort to resolve), and Test Patch Correctness (whether tests accurately verify the intended fix). Each task instance is assessed for each quality characteristic separately using a 75/25 training/validation split.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited exclusively to Python repositories, restricting diversity across programming languages. Only repositories with permissive licenses are included. The automated quality assessment is trained on SWE-bench Verified annotations, which may introduce biases from that dataset's manual curation. The pipeline may favor repositories with well-structured installation instructions, potentially underrepresenting older or less-documented projects.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks are collected from GitHub repositories via a four-stage automated pipeline: (1) preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub (downloading ~450,000 pull requests linked to issues from over 30,000 repositories with permissive licenses where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase); (2) automated installation instruction configuration using LLM-driven steps; (3) execution-based installation verification in containers; and (4) automated instance quality assessment using a fine-tuned LLM.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The git tag command provides a version for approximately 95% of task instances; the remaining ~5% are assigned a unique version so each uses its own environment. Flaky tests with external API calls or floating-point precision issues are excluded by running tests multiple times. Tasks with unpinned/obsolete dependencies that cannot be resolved are excluded. Tasks requiring interactive installation are excluded.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of GitHub pull requests linked to issues, collected from GitHub Archive (daily JSON archives of GitHub events) and directly cloned GitHub repositories. The primary data includes issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, metadata (creation date, labels), pull request merge status, last commit, discussions, and full commit histories.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025; benchmark subset focuses on issues created in 2025 (January and March–April 2025 subsets used for evaluation).
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: 1) Automated task quality assessment may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. 2) Limited language diversity: initial release is limited exclusively to Python. 3) LLM-based installation recipe generation was validated on only 18 repositories and may not capture every project's subtleties. 4) Automated quality assessment cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Tasks are grouped by project versions normalized to major.minor format. For each version group, the base_commit of the most recent pull request is selected. Patches are split into solution patch (non-test files) and test patch (test files only). Execution-based verification ensures tests fail before and pass after applying the solution patch. Flaky tests (involving external API calls or floating-point precision issues) are excluded by running tests multiple times.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering criteria applied: (1) Python repository with permissive license; (2) issue marked as resolved; (3) PR merged into main branch; (4) PR not linked to multiple issues; (5) issue description longer than 10 characters; (6) PR introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files; (7) changes affect 1 to 15 files. Each PR patch is divided into a solution patch (non-test files) and a test patch (test files only). Project versions are normalized to major.minor format. Dependency versions are frozen after successful setup via pip freeze and conda env export.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and benchmark are continuously updated with fresh tasks. A public leaderboard at https://swe-rebench.com/leaderboard is continuously updated with decontaminated evaluations. Future work includes expanding data coverage to non-issue-linked PRs, supporting new programming languages (JavaScript, Java, C++), and maintaining evaluation on fresh tasks for existing and new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may accelerate development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, bringing potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors believe fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.
rai:dataUseCases: Training LLM-based software engineering agents via reinforcement learning; benchmarking and evaluating LLM-based agents on real-world software engineering tasks; decontaminated evaluation of SWE agents; fine-tuning open-source models for software engineering tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (used for generating installation recipes and for automated quality assessment after fine-tuning on SWE-bench Verified annotations). The model generates up to three candidate JSON installation recipes per task and predicts quality labels (Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness).

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations per item; quality labels are predicted once per quality dimension by the fine-tuned model.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are automated (LLM-based); no human annotator demographics are described for the SWE-rebench dataset itself (SWE-bench Verified human annotations are used only for training the quality classifier).
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol for missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of GitHub issues, pull requests, and code patches; no personal or sensitive information collection is discussed.

evidence.name: we introduce a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline to continuously extract real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories. Using this pipeline, we construct SWE-rebench, a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks
evidence.description: SWE-rebench, a public dataset of more than 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches.
evidence.datePublished: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2505.20411v2 [cs.SE] 4 Nov 2025
evidence.inLanguage: Problem statement language: The problem statement must be in English.
evidence.citeAs: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
evidence.isLiveDataset: SWE-rebench uses an automated pipeline from Section 2 for a continuous supply of fresh tasks. Since we precisely track the creation dates of the issues and their corresponding pull requests against model release dates, we can explicitly mark potentially contaminated evaluations
evidence.rai:dataCollection: To initiate the dataset building process, we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025. These originate from over 30,000 repositories that feature permissive licenses granting broad usage rights and where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase lines of code.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive and GitHub. The GitHub Archive is a major source of public events on GitHub. Each day, it publishes a JSON archive listing all GitHub events from that day. We use this archive to collect detailed data about issues. We also clone relevant GitHub repositories with their full commit histories to our local storage.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The GitHub Archive is a major source of public events on GitHub. Each day, it publishes a JSON archive listing all GitHub events from that day. We use this archive to collect detailed data about issues: issue description, discussion, linked pull requests, and metadata such as creation date and labels. We also extract information about pull requests, including their merge status, last commit, and discussions.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025. These originate from over 30,000 repositories that feature permissive licenses granting broad usage rights
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We then link issues with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description, applying filters to select instances where: The issue is from a Python repository with a permissive license. The issue is marked as resolved. The PR is merged into the main branch. The PR is not linked to multiple issues. The issue description is longer than 10 characters. The PR must introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files. Changes affect 1 to 15 files.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: To assess these properties automatically, we fine-tune an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict: Issue Clarity: Whether the GitHub issue description is sufficiently detailed for a developer to understand and solve the problem. Task Complexity: The estimated effort to resolve the issue, considering reasoning, code modification, and codebase familiarity. Test Patch Correctness: Whether tests in the pull request accurately verify the intended fix without over-reliance on specific implementation details.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For Task Complexity (where 'high-score' implies >1 hour to solve; 100 high-score vs. 313 low-score examples in validation), our fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and a weighted F1-score of 0.82. This is an improvement over the baseline Qwen-72B-Instruct, which achieved 68% accuracy. For Test Patch Correctness (180 high-score vs. 233 low-score examples), the model achieved 67% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.65). For Issue Clarity (84 high-score vs. 329 low-score examples), it achieved 79% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.76).
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We use the Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct model to generate up to three candidate JSON recipes per task. If an error occurs during the subsequent scripted installation or test execution (derived from a recipe), the LLM attempts to refine that recipe by analyzing error logs and the original instructions.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: Automated task quality assessment: While we employ automated quality assessment, the fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue. This can lead to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. Limited language diversity: The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: SWE-rebench, a public dataset of more than 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: while our benchmark is intended to support transparency and standardization in evaluating SWE agents, it may also accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. We believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We group these task instances by project versions inferred from git tag outputs, normalizing versions to major.minor format (e.g., 1.2.3 is normalized to 1.2). For each version group, we select the base_commit of the pull request linked to the task instance with the most recent base_commit date.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The git tag command provides a version for approximately 95% of task instances. We assign a unique version to the rest of the tasks, so that each one of them uses its own environment.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The computationally intensive nature of our pipeline is managed through a distributed storage and computing platform TractoAI, which provides capabilities for efficient parallel processing and data management, helping us optimize throughput of each stage to enable rapid reprocessing whenever we change the pipeline.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Limited language diversity: The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems. Although the underlying pipeline is language-agnostic, adapting it to support other languages (such as Go, Java, Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript) requires implementing language-specific components, which is planned for future work.
evidence.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A public SWE-rebench leaderboard that offers continuously updated, decontaminated, and standardized evaluations for LLM-based agents, promoting transparency and fair comparisons across both open- and closed-source models. As the leaderboard is continuously updated, the current set of evaluated models can be found on the leaderboard website.
